questions.stem: When creating an alert management rule, where would you specify a workflow to resolve a given condition?
questions.explanation: In an alert management rule, you specify a workflow to resolve a given condition from the Actions tab (B). The Actions tab defines what the rule does when conditions are met, including triggering orchestration workflows. The Remediation tab (A) is specifically for CI remediation orchestration, not general workflow-based condition resolution. Launcher (C) and Related Links (D) are not alert management rule tabs.

questions.stem: What types of system can a MID Server install on? (Choose two.)

options.text: Any system inside the customer firewall

questions.explanation: A MID Server can be installed on Microsoft Windows Server (B) and Linux System (C). These are the two supported operating systems for MID Server installations. OpenVMS (A) and Mac OS X (F) are not supported. Microsoft Windows Desktop (D) is not a supported server OS. Any system inside the firewall (E) is incorrect — the OS must be Windows Server or Linux.

questions.stem: What would be the primary use case for creating Javascripts in Event Management?

options.text: To create a customized pull connector to retrieve events on behalf of an event source
To automatically populate the Configuration Management Database (CMDB)
To parse a nodename out of your raw event data in an event rule
To run as part of a remediation workflow for IT alerts that fail to execute

questions.explanation: The primary use case for creating JavaScript in Event Management is to create a customized pull connector to retrieve events on behalf of an event source (A). JavaScript connectors allow Event Management to pull events from external monitoring systems that lack built-in connectors. Populating CMDB (B) is handled by Discovery. Parsing node names (C) uses event rule transforms. Remediation workflow scripting (D) is done in Orchestration.

questions.stem: What would you use to define the monitoring sources allowed to communicate with the ServiceNow instance for Operational Intelligence?
questions.explanation: Metric Type Actions (C) are used to define the monitoring sources allowed to communicate with the ServiceNow instance for Operational Intelligence. Metric Type Actions configure which metric types from which sources are accepted and how they are processed. Metric Registration (A) is for registering metric definitions. Metric Config Rules (B) configure metric behavior. Metric to CI (D) handles metric-to-CI binding.

questions.stem: The value of the Alert Priority score is a composite of what?

options.text: The value of the alert’s category and its relative weight
The value of the alert’s category and its Priority Group
The value of the alert’s Severity and its Priority Group
The value of the alert’s Severity and its relative weight

questions.explanation: The Alert Priority score is a composite of the alert's category and its relative weight (A). Per the docs: 'Each category has its own placement in the alert priority score, according to its order and limit' — each category contributes a weighted value to compute the overall priority score. Priority Group (B) is a separate field. Severity (C, D) influences some categories but is not the direct composite formula for the priority score.

questions.stem: Which attribute is responsible for de-duplication?
questions.explanation: The message_key attribute (B) is responsible for de-duplication of events. Per the docs: 'message_key: This value is used for de-duplication of events.' Per the docs: 'The message_key field is a unique identifier for an alert in the source monitoring system. It is used for de-duplication and alert flapping detection.' Metric_name (A), short_description (C), and additional_info (D) are not de-duplication attributes.

questions.stem: How would you interpret the following data in the Operational Intelligence Insights Explorer?

options.text: win-ces882ierw is one of your hottest Configuration Items (CIs) that is currently experiencing a high probability of anomalies and should be checked immediately
win-ces882ierw is one of your hottest Configuration Items (CIs), but is currently experiencing a low probability of anomalies
win-ces882ierw is one of your customized list of monitored Configuration Items (CIs) that is currently experiencing a high probability of anomalies and should be checked immediately
win-ces882ierw is one of your customized list of monitored Configuration Items (CIs), but is currently experiencing a low probability of anomalies

questions.explanation: win-ces882ierw is one of the hottest CIs (highest anomaly tracking activity) but is currently experiencing a low probability of anomalies (B). Per the docs, green indicator means 'Metric for CI had at least one anomaly in the past, but anomaly score is currently 0' — indicating past activity but currently low probability. Hottest CIs are system-identified top CIs, not a customized list (eliminating C and D).

questions.stem: What is the default collection/polling interval applied to all event connectors?
questions.explanation: The default collection/polling interval applied to all event connectors is every 120 seconds (A). This is the standard default connector execution interval in Event Management. The 5-second interval (B) applies to the event processing job, not connectors. 40 seconds (C), 60 seconds (D), and 10 seconds (E) are not the default connector polling interval.

questions.stem: Where can you look to determine what event rule created an alert? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: You can determine what event rule created an alert by looking at the Alert Activity (A) which records the creation actions, and the Event Processing Notes (C) which shows which event rule processed and matched the event. Per the docs, the Activities tab records what happened to the alert. Event Additional Information (B), Alert Message Key (D), and Alert Source (E) do not show which event rule created the alert.

questions.stem: What feature would you use to trigger a workflow or automatically generate tasks via templates?
questions.explanation: Alert management rules (C) are used to trigger a workflow or automatically generate tasks via templates. Per the docs, alert management rules define conditions and actions including creating incidents, triggering workflows, and generating tasks automatically. Event rules (A) process events into alerts. Task rules (B) is not a standard EM module. Alert correlation rules (D) group related alerts.

questions.stem: What are the valid states an alert can be in during its lifecycle?
questions.explanation: The valid states an alert can be in are Open, Reopen, Flapping, and Closed (A). Per -3787, these are the documented alert lifecycle states: Open on creation, Reopen when reopened, Flapping when events continue after closure, and Closed when resolved. Options B, C, and D include invalid state names (Updating, Waiting, Swinging, Warning, Clear).

questions.stem: What Event Management module allows for configuration of automatic task creation?
questions.explanation: Alert management rules (A) is the Event Management module that allows configuration of automatic task creation. Alert management rules define conditions and specify automated actions including creating incidents and tasks from templates. Event rules (C) transform events into alerts. Alert correlation rules (D) group alerts. Task rules (B) is not a standard EM module.

questions.stem:
You have a system configured with a MID Web Server using Basic authentication to enable Operational Management Intelligence (OI) to push raw metric data to the MID Server. No data is getting through to the MID Server.
What is the most likely cause of the issue?

options.text: The MID Web Server needs to be Restarted
The MID Web Server needs to be Started
An invalid secret key is being passed in the header information of the URL for the REST request
An invalid password is set in the MID Web Server Context

questions.explanation: The most likely cause is an invalid password set in the MID Web Server Context (D). When using Basic authentication, the MID Web Server Context stores the username and password used to authenticate incoming requests. An invalid password causes all authentication attempts to fail, preventing data from reaching the MID Server. Restarting (A) or Starting (B) would address service state issues. Invalid secret key (C) applies to key-based auth, not Basic auth.

questions.stem: In the event table, which field maps the external attributes from the target system?
questions.explanation: The Additional Information field (D) in the event table maps the external attributes from the target system. This field stores supplementary data from the external monitoring source that doesn't map directly to standard event fields. Resource (A) identifies the monitored resource. Description (B) is the event description. Source (C) identifies the monitoring tool origin.

questions.stem: By default, the Alert Console displays what type of alerts?

options.text: All Primary, Open alerts and anomaly alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, and Warning that are not in Maintenance mode
All Primary and Secondary Open alerts and anomaly alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, and Warning that are not in Maintenance mode
All Primary alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, Warning that are not in Maintenance mode
All Primary, Open alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, and Warning that are not in Maintenance mode
All Primary and Secondary Open alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, and Warning that are not in Maintenance mode

questions.explanation: By default the Alert Console displays all Primary, Open alerts with a Severity of Critical, Major, Minor, and Warning that are not in Maintenance mode (D). Secondary alerts are excluded from the default view. Anomaly alerts (A, B) are a separate display type. Option C omits the Open/Maintenance filter. Option E incorrectly includes Secondary alerts.

questions.stem: Which are recommended best practices for Event Management? (Choose three.)

options.text: Filter out events on ServiceNow Instance for easier consolidation and aggregation.
Promote all events to alerts during initial implementation until you fully understand which should be ignored.
Filter out events at source rather than in the ServiceNow instance.
Base-line “normal-state” events to filter out background noise.
Ignore all non-critical events during initial implementation to streamline processing; add alerts over time as time and resources allow.

questions.explanation: Three recommended best practices are: Filter out events at source rather than in ServiceNow (C), Baseline normal-state events to filter background noise (D), and Ignore non-critical events during initial implementation (E). Filtering at source (C) reduces load on the instance. Baselining (D) establishes normal behavior. Starting with minimal scope (E) allows controlled rollout. Filtering in ServiceNow (A) is less efficient. Promoting all events to alerts (B) creates noise.

questions.stem: For an incoming event with a matching message key, what allows an existing alert to be automatically closed?

options.text: In the event rule, set the Severity to 0
In the alert rule, set the Severity to 0
In the alert rule, set the Severity to -1
In the event rule, set the Severity to -1

questions.explanation: Setting the Severity to 0 in the event rule (A) allows an existing alert to be automatically closed when an incoming event has a matching message key. Severity 0 represents a Clear/Resolved state, which triggers automatic closure of the matching alert. This must be set in the event rule (not alert rule), so B and C are incorrect. Severity -1 (C, D) is not a valid closure mechanism.

questions.stem:
A support agent resolves an incident associated with an alert, but the alert does automatically close even though the evt_mgmt.incident_closes_alert property is set appropriately to close the alert.
What is the most likely cause of this issue?

options.text: The support agent does not have the evt_mgmt_user role.
The support agent only has the evt_mgmt_admin role.
The support agent has the evt_mgmt_operator role, but not the evt_mgmt_user role.
The support agent has the evt_mgmt_user role, but not the evt_mgmt_operator role.

questions.explanation: The most likely cause is that the support agent does not have the evt_mgmt_user role (A). Per the docs, resolving an incident to close the associated alert requires the evt_mgmt_admin, evt_mgmt_operator, or evt_mgmt_user role. Without any of these roles, the property cannot execute the alert closure. Having only evt_mgmt_admin (B) would still work. Having operator without user (C) would still work. Option D is incorrect as evt_mgmt_user alone is sufficient.

questions.stem: What are the two most accurate statements regarding the ServiceNow CMDB (configuration management database) and CIs (configuration items)?

options.text: The CMDB is a series of tables that contain only key hardware components located in critical paths within your platform that must be managed.
The CMDB is a dynamic list that tracks both the CIs within your platform and the relationship between those items.
All CIs stored in the CMDB must have an assigned IP address within your infrastructure.
A CI is any component within your infrastructure that needs to be managed in order to deliver Services.

questions.explanation: The CMDB is a dynamic list that tracks CIs and their relationships (B), and a CI is any component that needs to be managed to deliver Services (D). B accurately describes the CMDB as a relational dynamic repository. D accurately defines a CI. CMDB contains more than just hardware (A is wrong). Not all CIs require IP addresses — software, services, and logical items have no IP (C is wrong).

questions.stem: What would you use as a central location to explore the CMDB class hierarchy, CI table definitions, and CIs?
questions.explanation: The CI Class Manager (E) is the central location to explore the CMDB class hierarchy, CI table definitions, and CIs. Per the docs: 'To access rules at the class level, use the CI Class Manager. Navigate to All > Configuration > CI Class Manager.' It provides a unified view of the entire CI class structure. CI Remediations (A), CI Relation Types (B), CI Identifiers (C), and Process to CI Type Mapping (D) are more specialized tools.

questions.stem:
A four node cluster makes up the components (CIs) of a Business Service. The impact influence for the cluster is set to 60%.
How many members of the cluster must be in a Critical state in order for the Business Service to display as Critical in the Impact Tree?
questions.explanation: 2 members (B) of the 4-node cluster must be in a Critical state for the Business Service to display as Critical. With a 60% impact influence per member, 2 Critical members × 60% = 120%, which exceeds 100% and triggers a Critical state on the Business Service. A single member (A) at 60% is insufficient. 3 (C) or 4 (D) members exceed what is needed.

questions.stem: Which the following alert promotion rule defined in your ServiceNow instance, which of the anomalies below would be automatically promoted into IT alerts on the Alert Console?

options.text: Both anomaly A and anomaly B
Neither anomaly A or anomaly B

questions.explanation: Anomaly B would be automatically promoted into an IT alert based on the alert promotion rule (B). This question references a visual/table showing promotion rule thresholds that is not available in the raw text. Community consensus indicates B based on the promotion rule criteria shown in the original question image.

questions.stem: By default, Event Management tries to bind an alert to CI (configuration item), by matching the node name in the event to which three items in the CMDB (configuration management database)?

options.text: CI name, Fully qualified domain name, IP or MAC address
CI name, Webserver name, IP or MAC address
CI name, Fully qualified domain name, SSH public host keys
System class name, Fully qualified domain name, IP or MAC address

questions.explanation: By default, Event Management binds an alert to a CI by matching the node name against the CI name, Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN), and IP or MAC address (A). Per the docs: 'the node value from the event is compared with various attributes in the host CI, such as Name, FQDN, IP, or MAC address.' Webserver name (B), SSH keys (C), and System class name (D) are not default binding attributes.

questions.stem: The MID Server requires an outbound connection on which port?
questions.explanation: The MID Server requires an outbound connection on port 443 (C), the standard HTTPS port. MID Servers communicate with the ServiceNow instance over HTTPS/443. Port 445 (A) is Windows file sharing. Port 161 (B) is SNMP. Port 143 (D) is IMAP.

questions.stem: If more than one event rule applies to a particular event or metric, which of the event rules will run based upon the Order of execution number?

options.text: Only the event rule with the highest Order of execution number will run.
Only the event rule with the lowest Order of execution number will run.
All event rules will run, from the lowest to the highest Order of execution numbers.
All event rules will run, from the highest to the lowest Order of execution numbers.

questions.explanation: All event rules run from lowest to highest Order of execution number (C). Per the docs: 'The event rules run in ascending order as defined in the Order field.' Multiple matching rules execute sequentially in ascending order unless restricted by the 'Apply additional matching rules' setting. Only the highest Order (A) or only lowest Order (B) running would prevent multiple rules from executing.

questions.stem: When creating event rules, is it best practice to create:
questions.explanation: The best practice is to create as few event rules as possible (C). Per the docs: 'Using a web service API for integration can reduce the number of event rules needed.' Fewer, broader rules are easier to maintain and perform better. Creating two rules per event (A), as many as possible (B), or one per event (D) all lead to rule sprawl and increased processing overhead.

questions.stem: During processing of the event and if the event Severity is blank, the state of the event is set to:
questions.explanation: If the event Severity is blank, the state of the event is set to Error (C). Per the docs, the Error state is applied when the event cannot be processed successfully — a missing Severity field causes a processing failure. Ready (A) is the initial waiting state. Ignored (B) is when an ignore rule applies. Processing/Processing (D) is not a valid final event state.

questions.stem: What two key steps must be performed after creating a new connector instance? (Choose two.)

options.text: Assign a MID Server to the connector

questions.explanation: After creating a new connector instance, the two key steps are: Test the connector (D) and Activate the connector (E). Per the docs: 'Select Test Connector' to verify the connection, then Activate to enable event collection. Assigning a MID Server (A) and entering credentials (B) are done during creation. Debugging (C) is not a required post-creation step.

questions.stem:
A customer informs you that they already have monitoring and event management tools.
Which of the following describes the extra value that ServiceNow Event Management provides? (Choose four.)

options.text: ServiceNow Event Management Alerts, Incidents, Problems, and changes are automatically correlated with CIs and Business Services that can be visualized in Business Service maps.
ServiceNow Event Management manages relationships between alerts and related incidents to maintain an end-to-end event management lifecycle.
ServiceNow Event Management provides a business-centric platform and single system of record for service monitoring and remediation results, to better control and manage performance and availability.
ServiceNow Event Management provides state-of-the-art performance monitoring capabilities across a wide array of different types of infrastructures.

ServiceNow Event Management utilizes the power of MID Servers provide important functions in your ITOM Health deployment. What does MID stand for? A. Management, Instrumentation. and Discovery B. Messaging. Integration, and Data C. Monitoring. Insight. and Domain D. Maintenance, Information, and Distribution with leading monitoring systems to automatically create actionable alerts.

questions.explanation: Four extra values ServiceNow EM provides are: Alerts/incidents/problems/changes correlated with CIs and Business Services (A), managing alert-to-incident relationships end-to-end (B), a business-centric single system of record (C), and MID Server integration with leading monitoring systems (E). State-of-the-art performance monitoring (D) describes what external tools do — EM's value is in correlation and consolidation, not raw monitoring.

questions.stem: You have an event with a Source of ‘Trap from Enterprise 111’, but the alert created for this event shows a Source of ‘Oracle EM’. If you want to change what this is set to, where in the event rule would you do this?

options.text: Transform and Compose Alert Output lab

questions.explanation: To change what the alert Source is set to, you would configure it in the Transform and Compose Alert Output tab (A) of the event rule. Per the docs: 'Since there is no existing name attribute in the event, we can manually create one using the Transform and Compose Alert Output tab in the event rule.' This tab is where alert field values are mapped and overridden from event data. Event Filter (D) matches events. CI Binding (C) handles CI association.

questions.stem: Copies of checks that have been included in Agent Client Collector policies are known as what?
questions.explanation: Copies of check definitions included in Agent Client Collector policies are known as check instances (E). Per the docs: 'You associate check definitions with policies. Those check definitions are then referred to as check instances' once they are part of a policy. Check definitions (A) are the original templates. Check models (B), clones (C), and mirrors (D) are not valid ACC terminology.

questions.stem: How often do baseline event connectors retrieve events?
questions.explanation: Baseline event connectors retrieve events every 2 minutes (B) by default. This is the standard connector execution interval in Event Management, equivalent to 120 seconds. Every 30 seconds (A) and every 5 seconds are for other EM scheduled jobs. Every 10 minutes (C) is too slow. Every 1 minute (D) and every 5 minutes (E) are not the baseline connector default.

questions.stem: Which attribute correlates multiple events to one alert?
questions.explanation: The message_key attribute (B) correlates multiple events to one alert. Per the docs: 'Where both events must be mapped to the same ServiceNow alert, they should have the same message key.' The message_key ensures that successive events about the same condition update the same alert rather than creating new ones. Additional_info (A), metric_name (C), and short_description (D) do not perform event correlation.

questions.stem: What attribute is used to consolidate events into a single alert?
questions.explanation: The Message Key attribute (B) consolidates events into a single alert. Events with the same Message Key are deduplicated into one alert, keeping it updated rather than creating duplicate alerts. Event Rules (A) process events but don't consolidate them — that's the message_key's role. Alert Priority (C) and Severity (D) are alert attributes, not consolidation keys.

questions.stem: Which attribute within an event needs to be exactly the same to allow for deduplication?
questions.explanation: The Message Key attribute (B) must be exactly the same across events to allow for deduplication into a single alert. Per the docs: events with matching message keys are mapped to the same alert. Metric Name (A) is used for metric identification. Type & Node (C) contribute to the auto-generated message key if left blank. Description (D) and Correlation ID (E) do not drive deduplication.

questions.stem: In default configuration using baseline connectors, how often is event data collected from event sources?
questions.explanation: In default configuration using baseline connectors, event data is collected every 2 minutes (B). This is the default connector execution interval (120 seconds). Once every minute (A) and twice every minute (C) are faster than the default. Every 5 minutes (D) is slower than the default baseline connector interval.

questions.stem: What applications are included in the ITOM Health product?
questions.explanation: ITOM Health includes Event Management and Operational Intelligence (A). These two applications — Event Management for alert correlation and Operational Intelligence (Metric Intelligence) for anomaly detection — form the ITOM Health/AIOps product. ITOM Visibility (B) includes Discovery and Service Mapping (C). Cloud Management (D) is a separate ITOM product.

questions.stem: What is one of the main benefits of using Event Management and Operational Intelligence?

options.text: To improve service availability by helping IT staff pinpoint service issue causes and evaluate the impact of planned changes.
To increase service agility and produce fast, predictable results by automating manual, routine, error-prone tasks.
To rapidly configure and launch secure, agentless discovery of hardware and software resources and their relationships.
To proactively warn against possible service outages using a range of advanced predictive machine learning methods.

questions.explanation: The main benefit of Event Management and Operational Intelligence is to proactively warn against possible service outages using advanced predictive machine learning methods (D). Per the docs, Metric Intelligence uses ML to identify anomalous CI behavior before outages occur. Improving service availability via issue pinpointing (A) and automation (B) are ITSM benefits. Agentless discovery (C) is a Discovery benefit.

questions.stem:
MID Servers provide important functions in your ITOM Health deployment.
What does MID stand for?
questions.explanation: MID stands for Management, Instrumentation, and Discovery (A). This is the official ServiceNow acronym for the MID Server, reflecting its three core functions: managing connections, instrumenting monitoring, and supporting discovery. The other options (B, C, D) are incorrect expansions of the acronym.

questions.stem: Out-of-the-box, how often do the events get processed in ServiceNow?

options.text: Every minute via a scheduled job
As soon as the event record is inserted via a business rule

questions.explanation: Out-of-the-box, events get processed every 5 seconds (A). Per the docs, the Event Management event processing job runs every 5 seconds. This near-real-time processing ensures rapid alert generation from incoming events. Every minute via scheduled job (B) is too slow. Processing via business rule on insert (C) is not how EM processes events. The frequency is not connector-dependent (D).

questions.stem:
HOTSPOT -
In what sequence are events processed?
questions.explanation: Events are processed in this sequence: (1) Event received and stored in em_event, (2) Event rules applied — ignore check, transforms, threshold accumulation, (3) Event field mapping applied, (4) CI binding performed, (5) Alert created or updated, (6) Alert management rules evaluated. This is a HOTSPOT sequence question with no visible options; sequence based on platform knowledge.

questions.stem: Which is not a valid method for accessing alert intelligence?

options.text: In the right-click menu of an alert list, select Open in Workspace
By appending/workspace to your instance URL
The application navigator Alerts Console menu item
The application navigator Alert Intelligence menu item
Within an open alert record, click the Open in Workspace button
Select the Lists tab in operator workspace

questions.explanation: 'The application navigator Alerts Console menu item' (C) is NOT a valid method for accessing alert intelligence. There is no 'Alerts Console' module in the application navigator for alert intelligence. Valid methods include: right-click menu Open in Workspace (A), appending /workspace to the URL (B), the Alert Intelligence navigator item (D), the Open in Workspace button on an alert (E), and the Lists tab in operator workspace (F).

questions.stem: To determine the top incidents for the CI associated with an alert, where is the best place to look?
questions.explanation: Alert Insights (A) is the best place to determine the top incidents for the CI associated with an alert. Alert Insights provides a consolidated view of related incidents, changes, and problems for the CI associated with an alert, enabling quick root cause analysis. Incident List View (B) requires filtering. CMDB Health Dashboard (C) is CI-centric. Event Management Overview (D) shows overall EM status, not per-alert incident details.

questions.stem: Agent Client Collector is built on what framework that enables you to adopt and extend monitoring checks from the community?
questions.explanation: Agent Client Collector is built on the Sensu framework (B). Per the docs: 'The Agent Client Collector is built on a Sensu framework and comes installed with monitoring capabilities for servers, databases, application servers, and middleware. It also supports extending monitoring through additional checks from the Sensu community or Nagios-compatible plugins.' Icinga (A), SolarWinds (C), Nagios (D), and Zabbix (E) are not the ACC framework.

questions.stem: Based on the information shown, which of the following three alerts should be processed first?

options.text:
The Alert Priority score 3106020.001 was calculated according to the following factors, ordered by their respective priority (2018-06-01 19:34:01 GMT) Category (Score, Weight)
1. Business services – (3.0, 1000000)
2. Severity – (1.0, 100000)
3. CI type – (60.0, 100)
4. Role – (2.0, 10)
5. Secondary – (0)
6. State – (1.0, 0.001)

The Alert Priority score 4406020.001 was calculated according to the following factors, ordered by their respective priority (2018-05-31 20:04:47 GMT) Category (Score, Weight)
1. Business services – (4.0, 1000000.0)
2. Severity – (4.0, 100000.0)
3. CI type – (60.0, 100.0)
4. Role – (2.0, 10.0)
5. Secondary – (0)
6. State – (1.0, 0.001)

The Alert Priority score 3306020.001 was calculated according to the following factors, ordered by their respective priority (2018-05-31 19:56:54 GMT) Category (Score, Weight)
1. Business services – (3.0, 1000000.0)
2. Severity – (3.0, 100000.0)
3. CI type – (60.0, 100.0)
4. Role – (2.0, 10.0)
5. Secondary – (0)
6. State – (1.0, 0.001)
They should be processed in the order in which they were received.

questions.explanation: Alert B with priority score 4406020.001 (B) should be processed first. The highest Alert Priority score indicates the most urgent alert requiring immediate attention. Score 4406020.001 (B) > 3306020.001 (C) > 3106020.001 (A). Alerts are not processed in the order received (D) — the priority score determines processing order.

questions.stem: Applying recommended Event Management best practice guidelines, which of the following events should generate an alert?

options.text: Every event should generate an alert so you have the opportunity to resolve them all.
Only events that necessitate action should generate an alert.
Only the most critical events on every CI in the CMDB should generate an alert.
Every event on every critical CI in the CMDB should generate an alert.

questions.explanation: Only events that necessitate action should generate an alert (B). This is the fundamental EM best practice to reduce noise and alert fatigue. Generating alerts for every event (A) creates unnecessary noise. Restricting to only critical events per CI (C) may miss non-critical but actionable issues. Every event on every critical CI (D) would also create excessive noise.

questions.stem: What makes all ServiceNow metrics, tasks, services, configuration items, assets, people, locations, and information a single system of record for IT and business processes?

options.text: ServiceNow is installed within your datacenter providing you complete control
All applications are built on the Oracle database standard, providing uniformity across products
All applications that are built by ServiceNow utilize the same data model and code base
ServiceNow runs on supported Windows servers and is managed through Windows Update
A single table houses all data elements within ServiceNow
ServiceNow utilizes the AWS MariaDB cloud database structure, providing a single system of record

questions.explanation: All applications built by ServiceNow utilize the same data model and code base (C). This shared platform architecture is what makes ServiceNow a single system of record — all products share the same underlying data model, tables, and platform services. ServiceNow is SaaS-hosted (A is wrong), uses its own DB (B is wrong), and a single table doesn't house all data (E is wrong).

questions.stem:
You have a very large networking environment and have noticed that your event notifications are either not being triggered or are delayed.
What are best options to try to resolve this issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Ensure all Event Management – process events jobs are set to a Ready state
Verify that the Bucket field in the event table is set to zero (0)
Ensure multi-node event processing is disabled

questions.explanation: The best options are to ensure all Event Management process events jobs are in a Ready state (A) and to add additional event processor jobs (C). Per the docs, scaling up event processing jobs addresses high event volume performance issues. Ensuring jobs are Ready ensures they execute properly. Setting Bucket to 0 (B) is not a standard solution. Disabling multi-node processing (D) would worsen the issue — enabling it would help.

questions.stem: What event value will auto close an alert?
questions.explanation: An event with a Resolution State of 'Closing' (C) will automatically close the corresponding alert. Per the docs: 'Closing event state closes corresponding alerts.' This is the event-level value that triggers alert closure. Severity 0/Clear (E) and Severity -1/OK (A) are event rule configurations that can also close alerts, but the event value that auto-closes is the Resolution State of Closing.

questions.stem: Given the following Impact settings and Alerts in a three node cluster that makes up the components of a Business Service, what is the overall service health of this Business Service?
questions.explanation: Based on the impact settings shown in the question (image-dependent), the overall service health is Clear (F). This is a visual question referencing impact settings not available in text form. Community answer is F (Clear), suggesting the configured impact thresholds for the 3-node cluster are not met by the current alert states, resulting in a Clear/healthy overall service status.

questions.stem: What does Operational Intelligence proactively identify before they cause service outages?
questions.explanation: Operational Intelligence proactively identifies anomalies (E) before they cause service outages. Per the docs: 'Metric Intelligence indicates anomalous behavior of CIs which events might not capture.' By detecting metric anomalies through ML analysis of historical data, it identifies potential issues before they escalate. Missing CMDB data (A), defects (B), alert correlations (C), and orphaned CIs (D) are not what OI proactively identifies.

questions.stem: What is the function of the External Communication Channel (ECC) Queue? (Choose three.)

options.text: It is a connection point between a ServiceNow instance and the MID Server.
It contains probe records to be executed on the customer’s network.
It holds jobs that the MID Server needs to perform.
It is a connection point between a hardware CI on a customer’s network and the MID Server.
It contains records of CIs that the ServiceNow admin has submitted for entry into the CMDB.

questions.explanation: The three functions of the ECC Queue are: it is a connection point between ServiceNow and the MID Server (A), it contains probe records to be executed (B), and it holds jobs the MID Server needs to perform (C). Per the docs: 'The External Communication Channel (ECC) Queue is a connection point between your ServiceNow instance and other systems... most commonly a MID Server.' It is not between hardware CIs and MID Server (D), and does not hold CMDB submission records (E).

questions.stem: The correct regex to capture the name of the server in “the server webserver3.domain.com is down” would be:
questions.explanation: The correct regex to capture 'webserver3.domain.com' from 'the server webserver3.domain.com is down' is.*\s(\w+\.\w+\.\w+).* (C). This pattern matches any text, then whitespace, then captures three word-segments separated by dots (hostname.domain.tld). Per the docs, capture groups use parentheses. Option A is greedy and may not capture correctly. Option B has case mismatch and captures too broadly. Option D captures too much after 'the server'.

questions.stem: What is the recommended approach to normalizing data from a source system to the default values in Event Management?
questions.explanation: Event field mapping (A) is the recommended approach to normalizing data from a source system to the default values in Event Management. Per the docs: 'Use Event field mapping rules to map values from specific fields to values in other fields.' Per the docs, event field mapping rules are stored in the em_mapping_rule table and apply after event rules. Transform maps (B) are ITSM import tools. Alert management rules (C) handle alert responses. Business rules (D) are general automation.

questions.stem:
You have an event that needs to be bound to a non-host CI.
Which attribute needs to be removed from the Transform and Compose tab?
questions.explanation: To bind an event to a non-host CI, the Node attribute must be removed from the Transform and Compose tab (C). Per the docs: 'Bind to host - by populating the Node field.' The Node attribute triggers host-based CI binding. Removing it forces the system to use other CI identifiers to bind to non-host CIs like applications or services. Source Instance (A), Metric Name (B), and Resource (D) are used for other purposes and do not drive host binding.

questions.stem: When are anomaly alerts generated by Operational Intelligence displayed in alert intelligence?

options.text: When the statistical model threshold is breached
When they are promoted to IT alerts
When it is manually promoted in insights explorer
When the anomaly score is greater than 100

questions.explanation: Anomaly alerts are displayed in alert intelligence when they are promoted to IT alerts (B). Per the docs: 'Anomaly alerts are separate from the regular IT alerts, and are not displayed in the Service Operations Workspace. You can define an anomaly alert promotion rule to generate an IT alert.' Per the docs: 'Anomaly alerts can be promoted to regular IT alerts and appear on the Service Operations Workspace' (alert intelligence).

questions.stem: What are the possible actions available in alert management? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three possible actions in alert management are: Execute remediation subflows (A), Execute remediation workflows (B), and Launch applications (C). Per the docs: 'Configure the following action types: Remediation Subflows: Execute a subflow... Remediation Workflows... Launch Applications: Open applications and browsers.' Evaluate business rule (D) and create service catalog request (E) are not standard alert management action types.

questions.stem: What ServiceNow feature would you configure to process incoming email to create events?
questions.explanation: Inbound actions (B) are the ServiceNow feature configured to process incoming email and create events. Per the docs: 'Configure event collection from email... Configure an inbound email action to send email notifications when events and alerts are triggered.' Transforms (A) map data within the platform. Event processing jobs (C) process existing events. Event Filter (D) and Event field mapping (E) operate on events already in the system.

questions.stem: Within a PowerShell script, which two URI’s could you use to log events directly to the ServiceNow event table? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: The two valid URIs to log events directly to the ServiceNow event table are /api/global/em/jsonv2 (B) and /api/now/table/em_event (C). Per the docs: the EM-specific web service API uses /api/global/em/jsonv2 for batch event insertion. The standard Table API /api/now/table/em_event also supports direct event insertion. The other options (A, D, E) use invalid path structures not matching ServiceNow API conventions.

questions.stem: If more than one alert management rule applies to a particular alert, which of the rules will run based upon the Order of execution field?

options.text: Only the alert management rule with the highest Order of execution number will run.
Only the alert management rule with the lowest Order of execution number will run.
All alert management rules will run, from the lowest to the highest Order of execution numbers.
All alert management rules will run, from the highest to the lowest Order of execution numbers.

questions.explanation: All alert management rules run from lowest to highest Order of execution number (C). Per the docs: 'Automations run in order from the lowest' order number. Multiple matching alert management rules all execute sequentially in ascending order. Only running the highest Order (A) or lowest Order (B) would prevent multiple rules from firing. Rules do not run from highest to lowest Order (D).

questions.stem: Alerts are processed using which of the following? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: Alerts are processed using Alert management rules (A), Event rules (C), and Scheduled jobs (D). Alert management rules respond to alerts with actions; event rules create and transform alerts; scheduled jobs execute the processing pipeline. 'Event action rules' (B) are the legacy name for alert management rules, not a separate mechanism. Java and Groovy scripts (E) are not standard EM alert processing mechanisms.

questions.stem: The individual commands that the Agent Client Collector executes on the host are known as what? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The individual commands ACC executes produce Events (A), Checks (B), and Metrics (E). Per the docs: 'The commands and their configurations that run on the Agent are called checks.' Per the docs: checks 'collect various system metrics and events.' Checks (B) are the commands themselves, while Events (A) and Metrics (E) are the result types. Parameters (C), Policies (D), and Scripts (F) are not what ACC commands are called.

questions.stem: What is Event Management licensing based on?

options.text: The number of unique nodes that can send events to the instance
The number of connectors and listeners it will collect data from
The number of connectors it will collect data from
The number of CIs in the CMDB that it will be monitoring

questions.explanation: Event Management licensing is based on the number of CIs in the CMDB being monitored (D). Per the docs: 'CIs bound to alerts are counted towards licensing; if there are no CIs that are bound to alerts, the event node field is used.' Licensing counts monitored CIs, not just nodes (A), connectors (B/C), which are secondary metrics.

questions.stem: What missing attribute would cause an event to have a state of Error?
questions.explanation: A missing Severity attribute would cause an event to have an Error state (E). Per the docs: 'Error: Failure occurred while processing the event. For example, the event collection method or event Severity is blank.' Severity is required for event processing — without it the event cannot be evaluated and enters Error state. Metric Name (A), Source (B), Classification (C), and Node (D) missing do not directly trigger Error state.

questions.stem: Modified Agent Client Collector policies do not take effect until what action is taken?

options.text: The check is tested on an existing agent/host

questions.explanation: Modified ACC policies do not take effect until the policy is republished (B). Publishing distributes the updated policy configuration to agents via the MID Server. Testing a check (A), re-running discovery (C), MID Server synchronization (D), and restarting agents (E) do not apply policy changes — republishing is the required action to propagate modifications.

questions.stem: What does the Asynchronous Messaging Bus (AMB) channel do on the MID Server?

options.text: Opens an inbound connection to the MID Server
Allows Web Server transactions to be passed to ServiceNow
Sends heartbeat information to the ServiceNow instance to ensure MID is communicating
Continually queries the External Communication Channel (ECC) queue via a persistent query

questions.explanation: The Asynchronous Messaging Bus (AMB) channel on the MID Server continually queries the External Communication Channel (ECC) queue via a persistent query (D). The AMB maintains a persistent connection to the instance, enabling real-time notification of new work items without constant polling overhead. It does not open inbound connections (A), pass Web Server transactions (B), or send heartbeat data (C) — those are separate mechanisms.

questions.stem: Within the ServiceNow IT Operations Management solution set, which statement most accurately describes what Event Management is?

options.text: The process responsible for defining, analyzing, planning, measuring, and improving all aspects of the availability of IT services
The process responsible for ensuring the capacity of IT Services and IT infrastructure is able to deliver agreed upon service level targets in a cost-effective manner
The process responsible for monitoring all abnormal occurrences throughout the IT infrastructure, allowing for normal operations, and detecting and escalating exception conditions
The process responsible for recovery action and planning through machine learning

questions.explanation: Event Management is the process responsible for monitoring all abnormal occurrences throughout the IT infrastructure, allowing for normal operations, and detecting and escalating exception conditions (C). This is the standard ITIL/ITOM definition of event management. Availability management (A) and Capacity management (B) are separate ITIL processes. Recovery through ML (D) describes AI/OI capabilities, not EM's core definition.

questions.stem: When creating a task from an alert what Event Management Module would be used?
questions.explanation: Alert Management (D) is the EM module used when creating a task from an alert. Alert management rules configure automated actions including task and incident creation when alert conditions are met. Event Rules (A) process events into alerts. Alert Correlation Rules (B) group related alerts. Task Management (C) is not a standalone EM module for this purpose.

questions.stem: What is the preferred method of parsing in the Transform/Compose step of an event rule?
questions.explanation: Regex (B) is the preferred method of parsing in the Transform/Compose step of an event rule. Per the docs, the event rule designer has an explicit regex mode for parsing event data, with built-in UI support for building regex expressions from event field values. Python (A) and sed/awk (C) are not supported. JavaScript (D) is available but regex is the preferred/built-in approach for transform parsing.

questions.stem: What are the server requirements to allow Operational Intelligence to successfully collect operational metric data via a push?

options.text: This requires a minimum of three MID Servers - two for Event Management and one additional MID Server dedicated for use by Operational Intelligence (OI).
This requires a MID Web Server in addition to the MID Server.
Nothing additional is required; this is handled by the MID Server.
This requires a minimum of two MID Servers - one for Event Management and one additional MID Server dedicated for use by Operational Intelligence (OI).

questions.explanation: To collect metric data via push, a MID Web Server is required in addition to the standard MID Server (B). The MID Web Server extension provides an HTTP endpoint that monitoring sources can push data to. A single MID Server handles pull-based collection (C is wrong). Multiple dedicated MID Servers (A, D) describe distributed deployments, not the core push requirement.

questions.stem: What would be an appropriate use case for having to write JavaScript in Event Management?

options.text: To change the value of the message key
To create a custom action within a subflow
To parse a node name out of your raw event data in an event rule

questions.explanation: An appropriate use case for writing JavaScript in Event Management is to create a custom action within a subflow (B). Custom subflow actions use JavaScript to implement complex logic not achievable through configuration alone. Changing message key value (A) is done via event rule transforms. Parsing node names (C) is best done with regex (preferred method). Automatically creating incidents (D) is handled via alert management rules.

questions.stem: A dynamic grouping of CIs based upon common criteria (filtered CI classes) that can be visualized in operator workspace is called?
questions.explanation: A dynamic grouping of CIs based upon common criteria (filtered CI classes) that can be visualized in operator workspace is called a Technical service (B). Per the docs: 'A technical service is a dynamic grouping of CIs based on some common criteria. For example, a technical service could be comprised of all web servers or all Oracle databases for a specific location.' Application service (C) is a broader category. Manual service (D) is user-defined.

questions.stem: During CI binding, CI matching is done using which two fields? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: During CI binding, CI matching is done using the Additional Information field (B) and the Node field (D). Per the docs: 'the system considers all fields in the Additional Information field and attempts to match their values with the CI table.' Per the docs: 'the node value from the event is compared with various attributes in the host CI.' Message Key (A) is for deduplication. Source (C) identifies the monitoring tool, not for CI matching.

questions.stem: What three areas of data quality does the CMDB Health Dashboard focus on? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The three areas of data quality the CMDB Health Dashboard focuses on are Correctness (A), Completeness (B), and Compliance (F). These are the standard CMDB health dimensions: Completeness measures if all required attributes are populated, Correctness validates accuracy of data, and Compliance checks adherence to defined standards. Configuration (C), Conciseness (D), and Conformity (E) are not the CMDB Health Dashboard dimensions.

questions.stem: When sending data from the monitoring source to the additional_info field, what format is supported?
questions.explanation: JSON (B) is the supported format when sending data from the monitoring source to the additional_info field. Per the docs, the event additional_info field uses JSON format: '"additional_info":"{\"name\":\"My Airlines\"}".' XML (A), YAML (C), and comma-separated (D) are not the supported formats for the additional_info field.

questions.stem: Which step in the event rule configuration process enables you to ignore events and prevent alert generation?
questions.explanation: The Event filter step (B) in event rule configuration enables you to ignore events and prevent alert generation. The Event Filter tab defines matching conditions — when the Ignore check box is selected, matching events are not promoted to alerts. Transform and Compose (A) customizes alert content. Event Options (C) is not a standard tab name. Threshold (D) suppresses alerts until a count threshold is met.

questions.stem: What is an alert called that moves from an open to a closed state multiple times within a designated time-frame?
questions.explanation: An alert that moves from open to closed multiple times within a designated timeframe is called Flapping (D). Per the docs: flapping 'has fluctuated between a closed and a non-closed state within the flap interval.' Flapping indicates the underlying condition is unstable, possibly due to thresholds set too low. Fluctuating (A), Swinging (B), and Flipping (C) are not valid ServiceNow alert state names.

questions.stem: How would you ensure the quality of data in your Configuration Management Database (CMDB) over time?

options.text: Manually inventorying configuration items in the CMDB and eliminating duplicate configuration items (CIs)
Only use the ServiceNow Discovery application to populate your CMDB
Using only scripts to automatically monitor for and remediate duplicate configuration items (CIs)
Having well-defined Identification, Reconciliation, and Relationship rules

questions.explanation: Having well-defined Identification, Reconciliation, and Relationship rules (D) is the best approach for ensuring CMDB data quality over time. These rules prevent duplicate CIs, ensure accurate updates from multiple sources, and maintain correct relationships. Manual inventory (A) is unsustainable. Using only Discovery (B) or only scripts (C) are overly restrictive single-source approaches.

questions.stem: Which is an invalid state for an alert?
questions.explanation: Processed (D) is an invalid state for an alert. Valid alert states are Open, Reopen, Flapping, and Closed — as confirmed by -3787. Processed is an event state (for the em_event table), not an alert state. Flapping (A), Closed (B), and Reopen (C) are all valid alert lifecycle states.

questions.stem: A support agent resolves an incident associated with an alert. What is the best method to close the alert?

options.text: Switch over to the alert form and close the alert manually
Create a business rule on the alert table to match the associated Incident with its respective alert
Create a business rule on the incident table

questions.explanation: The best method to close an alert when a support agent resolves the associated incident is to set the evt_mgmt.incident_closes_alert property (A). Per the docs: 'When you resolve an incident that is associated with an alert, the alert can also close according to the evt_mgmt.incident_closes_alert property.' This property automates the closure. evt_mgmt.alert_closes_incident (B) works in the reverse direction. Manual closure (C) and business rules (D, E) are inefficient alternatives.

questions.stem: Impacted services for alerts are calculated using data from which table?
questions.explanation: Impacted services for alerts are calculated using data from the svc_ci_assoc table (D). Per the docs: 'Use the Service Configuration Item Association' table to create the service map for impact calculation. This table maps CIs to their associated application services for impact propagation. cmdb_ci_hardware (A), em_impacted_svc (B), and cmdb_ci_rei (C) are not the table used for service-CI association data.

questions.stem: A monitoring tool notification of a notable occurrence is known as what?
questions.explanation: A monitoring tool notification of a notable occurrence is known as an event (B). Events are raw notifications sent from external monitoring tools to ServiceNow. After event rules process these raw events, they are promoted to alerts. An alert (A) is a ServiceNow-created record derived from events. A metric (C) is a performance measurement. An alarm (D) is terminology from some external tools, not the ServiceNow EM term.

questions.stem: If a Message Key is not provided, which fields are concatenated to make our own?

options.text: Source, DNS, Node, Additional info, Metric Name
Source, Type, Node, Resource, Metric Name
Source, Type, DNS, Additional info, Metric Name
Source, Source Instance, Node, Type, Resource

questions.explanation: If a Message Key is not provided, the fields Source, Type, Node, Resource, and Metric Name (B) are concatenated to generate one. Per the docs: 'If this value is empty, it is generated from the Source, Node, Type, Resource, and Metric Name field values.' DNS (A, C) and Source Instance (D) are not part of the auto-generated message key formula.

questions.stem: A load balanced web application has a cluster of 5 Apache nodes. When considering impact calculation with application cluster member rule influence set to 45, how many impacted nodes within that cluster would cause the overall application service to have a degradation of service?
questions.explanation: 3 nodes (D) within the 5-node cluster must be impacted to cause overall service degradation with a 45% influence setting. 3 × 45% = 135%, which exceeds 100% and triggers degradation of the application service. 1 node (B) = 45% and 2 nodes (C) = 90% — both below the 100% threshold required for service degradation. All 5 (A) or 4 (E) nodes exceed what is needed.

questions.stem: A Service is not viewable in Operator Workspace. What could be the issue?

options.text: The service is a manual service
The service is not set to operational
The service was created through Service Mapping
The service is a technical service

questions.explanation: A service not viewable in Operator Workspace is most likely not set to operational (B). Services must have their operational status set to 'Operational' to appear in the Operator Workspace. Manual services (A), Service Mapping-discovered services (C), and technical services (D) are all displayable in Operator Workspace regardless of how they were created.

questions.stem: What ServiceNow feature is an aid to rapid implementation of your Event Management and Operational Intelligence features?
questions.explanation: Guided setup (D) is the ServiceNow feature that aids in rapid implementation of Event Management and Operational Intelligence. Per the docs: 'Event Management setup using guided setup provides a sequence of tasks that help you configure Event Management on your ServiceNow instance.' Deployment wizard (A), Step-by-step guide (B), and Checklist application (C) are not the ServiceNow feature name for this capability.

questions.stem: The ServiceNow standard and shared set of service-related definitions that enable and support true service level reporting is known as what?
questions.explanation: The Common service data model (D) is the standard and shared set of service-related definitions that enable and support true service level reporting. Per the docs: 'The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) helps you streamline service types and service offerings.' The CSDM is the ServiceNow standard for organizing service-related data across all applications. Service level (A), Business service (B), and Application service (C) data models are not the correct term.

questions.stem: A monitoring tool notification of a notable occurrence is known as what?
questions.explanation: A monitoring tool notification of a notable occurrence is known as an event (E). Events are the raw notifications received from external monitoring systems. An alarm (A) and alert (B) are different — alerts are created in ServiceNow after processing events through event rules. An incident (C) is an ITSM record. A notice (D) and metric (F) are different types of data.

questions.stem: Which is the best option to reduce latency issues when receiving events?

options.text: Verify bucket field in em_event table > 0

questions.explanation: Verifying the bucket field in the em_event table is greater than 0 (A) is the best option to reduce latency issues when receiving events. The bucket field enables batched parallel event processing — when set above 0, events are distributed across processing buckets for concurrent handling. event_processor_job_count = 2 (B) is insufficient context. Setting job count to 0 (C) would stop processing. multi_node = 2 (D) is not a valid property value.

questions.stem: The default polling time to collect events from an event source is:
questions.explanation: The default polling time to collect events from an event source is 120 seconds (D). Per the docs: 'Default schedule: The number of seconds between attempts to receive events' — the standard connector default is 120 seconds (2 minutes). This is consistent with the connector execution job interval. 5 seconds (A), 30 seconds (B), and 60 seconds (C) are not the default connector polling interval.

questions.stem: Which two methods can be used to improve the processing of events in large network environments? (Choose two.)

options.text: Ensure the bucket value in the event table is greater than 0
Increase the number of scheduled jobs processing events

questions.explanation: Two methods to improve event processing in large network environments are: Enable multi-node processing (A) and Increase the number of scheduled jobs processing events (D). Per the docs, scaling up involves adding more processing capacity. Multi-node processing (A) distributes load across nodes. More scheduled jobs (D) adds parallel processing capacity. Increasing polling interval (B) reduces event frequency. Bucket value > 0 (C) is for latency, not processing capacity.

questions.stem: The Event Management operator workspace can display all of the following except?

options.text: Discovered application services from Service Mapping

questions.explanation: The Event Management operator workspace cannot display Correlation groups (D). The operator workspace displays alert groups (A), manual application services (B), discovered application services from Service Mapping (C), and technical services (E). Correlation groups are an internal alert correlation mechanism and are not a displayable service type in the operator workspace.

questions.stem: Within an event rule, how would you parse a nodename out of your raw event data?
questions.explanation: Within an event rule, you would use a Regex statement (D) to parse a nodename out of raw event data. Per the docs, the event rule designer has a built-in regex mode specifically for parsing event fields, making it the preferred parsing approach. JavaScript (A) is available but not the recommended method for nodename parsing. Groovy (B) is deprecated. PowerShell (C) is not applicable within event rules.

questions.stem: If events are not matching to alerts as you would like, what field should be changed?
questions.explanation: If events are not matching to alerts as desired, the Message Key field (B) should be changed. The message key determines which events correlate to the same alert — events with matching message keys are consolidated into one alert. Adjusting the message key ensures correct event-to-alert mapping. Resource (A), Node (C), and Metric Name (D) affect other aspects of event processing but not event-to-alert matching/deduplication.

questions.stem: If the Message Key is not populated, the default value is created from which fields?

options.text: Source, type. node, resource, and metric name
Source, source instance, node, and resource
Source, type. node, and metric name
Source, source instance, node, and type
Source, type. node, resource, and time of event

questions.explanation: If the Message Key is not populated, the default value is created from Source, type, node, resource, and metric name (A). Per the docs: 'If this value is empty, it is generated from the Source, Node, Type, Resource, and Metric Name field values.' Source instance (B, D) and time of event (E) are not part of the auto-generated message key. The metric name is included (eliminating C).

questions.stem: Processing on an event will create a state of error if what value is not set?
questions.explanation: Processing creates an Error state if the Severity value is not set (C). Per the docs: 'Error: Failure occurred while processing the event. For example, the event collection method or event Severity is blank.' Severity is a required field for event processing. Node (A), Source (B), Message Key (D), and Resource (E) missing do not directly trigger Error state.

questions.stem: When performing CI Binding, what fields does Event Management match to the Node?

options.text: CI Name, DNS, IP, MAC Address
System class name, FQDN, IP or MAC address
CI name, FQDN, SSH public host keys
CI Name, FQDN, IP, MAC Address

questions.explanation: When performing CI Binding, Event Management matches the Node to CI Name, FQDN, IP, and MAC Address (D). Per the docs: 'The system compares the Node with attributes like Name, FQDN, IP, or MAC Address in the CMDB to find a match.' Option A uses DNS instead of FQDN. Option B has System class name instead of CI name. Option C has SSH keys instead of IP/MAC.

questions.stem: Applying recommended Event Management best practice guidelines, which of the following alerts should be processed first?
questions.explanation: Alert0010003 (B) should be processed first based on the highest Alert Priority score. This question references a visual/image showing alert priority data not available in text form. Per EM best practices, alerts with the highest priority score are processed first. Community consensus (100%) indicates B has the highest priority score among the listed alerts.

questions.stem: What is the minimum role needed to view alerts?
questions.explanation: The minimum role needed to view alerts is evt_mgmt_user (B). Per the docs: role required includes 'evt_mgmt_user' as the lowest level role that can view alerts. evt_mgmt_user is the view-only access role for Event Management. evt_mgmt_operator (C) has additional action capabilities but is not the minimum. alert_operator (A) and alert_user (D) are not standard EM roles.

questions.stem: By default, when are idle alerts are closed?
questions.explanation: By default, idle alerts are closed after 7 days (A). Per the docs, the 7-day threshold is referenced as the default interval after which closed alerts are not re-opened. The 30-day interval (C) applies to retaining open event data. 14 days (B) is not the default. Alerts are not kept indefinitely (D) — they are closed after the idle threshold.

questions.stem: What is used to correctly bind an alert to an application?
questions.explanation: CI identification rules (D) are used to correctly bind an alert to an application CI. Per the docs: when a matching application CI (e.g., IIS Web Server) is found on the host using CI identification rules, the alert is bound to the correct application CI rather than just the host machine. Correlation rules (A) group alerts. Workflows (B) automate responses. Classifiers (C) identify CI types during Discovery.

questions.stem: If you wanted to create a quick response alert rule to open an Ask Jeeves search on the description of the alert, where would it configured?
questions.explanation: To create a quick response alert rule that opens a web search on the alert description, you configure it under Launch Applications (A) in alert management rules. Per the docs: 'Launch Applications: Open applications and browsers that you configure.' This action type opens URLs and browser-based applications as a response to alerts. Remediation Workflows (B) and Subflows (C) execute automated tasks. Operator Workspace (D) is the UI view.

questions.stem: Where would you find the Priority Breakdown for an Alert?
questions.explanation: The Priority Breakdown for an alert is found under the More Information section (A) of the alert form. This section displays the calculated priority score breakdown showing the contribution of each category (Business services, Severity, CI type, Role, State) to the overall alert priority score. Activities (B) shows work history. History (C) shows event times. CI Problems (D) shows related CI issues.

questions.stem: Where does an operator give feedback on an automated alert grouping?

options.text: Feedback attribute on the virtual alert record
Feedback attribute on the child alert record
Feedback attribute on the event record
Feedback attribute on the alert record
Dropdown box on the alert group record

questions.explanation: An operator gives feedback on an automated alert grouping via the Feedback attribute on the alert record (D). Per the docs, the Feedback field is available on the alert form record where operators can indicate whether the automated grouping is correct or not. Per the docs: 'the feedback option is available but does not trigger further actions after being logged.' Virtual alert (A) and child alert (B) feedback attributes are not the standard location.

questions.stem: In your environment, no alert CMDB, automated, or text based grouping is occurring. What is most likely the problem?

options.text: No correlation rules have been defined
No event management rules have been defined
The alert correlation property that enables grouping is set to false

questions.explanation: If no CMDB, automated, or text-based grouping is occurring, the most likely cause is that the alert correlation property that enables grouping is set to false (E). Per the docs, each grouping type (CMDB, ML-based automation, text-based) has its own property that must be enabled. If the master correlation property is false, all grouping types are disabled. No correlation rules (A) would only affect rule-based grouping, not automated and text-based.

questions.stem: The additional information field is a JSON string that gives more information about an event. An example of a supported JSON string is:
questions.explanation: The supported JSON string format for the additional_info field is {"CPU":"100"} (D) — with string values in quotes. ServiceNow EM requires the additional_info field values to be strings (not raw integers). Option A has an integer value without quotes. Option B is malformed JSON. Option C has mixed types (string and integer). D with string values only is the correct supported format.

questions.stem: In order for SNMP trap notifications to appear in ServiceNow as events, what option must be enabled in the required MID server?

options.text: SNMP event manager module for MID

questions.explanation: For SNMP trap notifications to appear in ServiceNow as events, the MID SNMP trap listener (A) must be enabled on the required MID Server. Per the docs: 'Use the MID SNMP Trap Listener to listen for SNMP traps. In this configuration, the specified MID Server acts as a collection endpoint for SNMP traps.' SNMP event manager (B), event collector extension (C), and SNMP agent (D) are not the correct module names.

questions.stem: What event will cause Agent Client Collector self-monitoring to pause data collection?

options.text: Communication with the MID server is lost
The amount of host memory being used by the agent exceeds a threshold
Communication with the ServiceNow instance is lost
The amount of host disk space used by the agent exceeds a threshold
The amount of host CPU being utilized by the agent exceeds a threshold

questions.explanation: ACC self-monitoring pauses data collection when the amount of host CPU being utilized by the agent exceeds a threshold (E). This protects the host system from being overwhelmed by the monitoring agent's own resource consumption. Loss of MID server communication (A) or instance communication (C) would affect connectivity, not trigger a pause. Memory (B) and disk space (D) thresholds do not trigger collection pause.

questions.stem: Agent Client Collector can perform application service monitoring by configuring what option?
questions.explanation: ACC can perform application service monitoring by configuring a proxy agent (B). Per the docs, proxy agents allow ACC to monitor external services and CIs that are not on the local host — enabling application service monitoring. An alert management rule (A) handles alert responses. A distributed cluster (C) provides HA for agent monitoring. Event rule (D) processes events. A REST API (E) is not an ACC configuration option.
